```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1 import make_axes_locatable

# Phase C's low count cut. Phase B draws it as a marker so the plots show what it would
# remove; nothing is filtered here.
LOW_COUNT_CUT = 20

# What the workflow staged beside the notebook, told apart by file name suffix. The trailing
# comma raises unless exactly one matches.
(TABLE,) = Path(".").glob("*.create_spatialdata_cellpose.h5ad")
(FOV_EXTENTS,) = Path(".").glob("*.fov_extents.csv")
```

```{python}
# | tags: [helpers]
# Plotting only: every function here takes already-computed data and draws a figure.
# No AnnData indexing, aggregation or column derivation happens in this cell.


def plot_counts_per_cell(transcripts, genes, medians, low_cut, share_below_cut):
    """B2: transcripts per cell and genes per cell, as histograms over the full range."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    panels = [
        (transcripts, "Transcripts per cell", "transcripts", 8, True),
        (genes, "Genes per cell", "genes", 2, False),
    ]
    for ax, (x, title, name, width, mark_cut) in zip(axes, panels):
        # Integer-aligned bins: each holds the same number of whole counts, so there is
        # no comb pattern.
        ax.hist(x, bins=np.arange(-0.5, x.max() + width, width), color="0.35")
        ax.axvline(medians[name], color="tab:blue", lw=1.2, label=f"median {medians[name]:.0f}")
        if mark_cut:
            ax.axvline(
                low_cut,
                color="tab:red",
                lw=1.2,
                ls="--",
                label=f"Phase C cut ({low_cut}): {share_below_cut:.1%} of cells",
            )
        ax.set(title=title, xlabel=f"{name} per cell", ylabel="cells")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    return fig


def plot_cell_volume(volume, median, bin_width=20):
    """B3: cell volume, as a histogram over the full range."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.8, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.hist(volume, bins=np.arange(0, volume.max() + bin_width, bin_width), color="0.35")
    ax.axvline(median, color="tab:blue", lw=1.2, label=f"median {median:.0f} µm³")
    ax.set(title="Cell volume", xlabel="volume (µm³)", ylabel="cells")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    return fig


def plot_blank_codewords(gene_totals, blank_totals, cells_per_blank_count):
    """B4: blank codewords against real genes, per codeword and per cell."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    # Left: one dot per codeword, jittered sideways, with each group's median.
    ax = axes[0]
    groups = [(gene_totals, "0.35", "real genes"), (blank_totals, "tab:red", "blank codewords")]
    for x_, (totals, color, name) in enumerate(groups):
        ax.scatter(x_ + rng.uniform(-0.3, 0.3, len(totals)), totals, s=6, color=color, alpha=0.7, linewidths=0)
        ax.hlines(np.median(totals), x_ - 0.38, x_ + 0.38, color="tab:blue", lw=1.5)
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1], [f"real genes (n={len(gene_totals)})", f"blank codewords (n={len(blank_totals)})"])
    ax.set(title="Total counts per codeword", ylabel="counts across the section (log)", xlim=(-0.6, 1.6))

    # Right: how many cells have 0, 1, 2, ... blank counts; the first few are labelled.
    ax = axes[1]
    k = np.arange(len(cells_per_blank_count))
    ax.bar(k, cells_per_blank_count, width=0.9, color="0.35")
    for x_ in k[:4]:
        ax.text(x_, cells_per_blank_count[x_], f"{cells_per_blank_count[x_] / cells_per_blank_count.sum():.0%}",
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7)
    ax.set(title="Blank counts per cell", xlabel="blank counts in the cell", ylabel="cells")
    return fig


def plot_transcripts_on_tissue(xy, transcripts, vmax, x_profile, y_profile, x_bounds, y_bounds):
    """B5: transcript count drawn on tissue, with its mean along x and y at the margins.

    x_bounds and y_bounds are where the field-of-view columns and rows start and end.
    """
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7), constrained_layout=True)
    pts = ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=transcripts, s=0.4, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=vmax,
                     linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set(xlabel="x (µm)", ylabel="y (µm)")

    divider = make_axes_locatable(ax)
    ax_top = divider.append_axes("top", size="22%", pad=0.08, sharex=ax)
    ax_right = divider.append_axes("right", size="22%", pad=0.08, sharey=ax)
    cax = divider.append_axes("bottom", size="3%", pad=0.65)

    ax_top.plot(*x_profile, color="0.2", lw=0.8)
    for b in x_bounds:
        ax_top.axvline(b, color="red", lw=0.4, alpha=0.4)
    ax_top.set(ylabel="mean per cell")
    ax_top.tick_params(labelbottom=False)
    ax_top.set_title("Transcripts per cell on tissue")

    ax_right.plot(y_profile[1], y_profile[0], color="0.2", lw=0.8)
    for b in y_bounds:
        ax_right.axhline(b, color="red", lw=0.4, alpha=0.4)
    ax_right.set(xlabel="mean per cell")
    ax_right.tick_params(labelleft=False)

    fig.colorbar(pts, cax=cax, orientation="horizontal",
                 label=f"transcripts per cell (colour clipped at the 99th percentile, {vmax:.0f})")
    return fig
```

## B1. Load the section

The table is Phase A's output: raw counts for the 491 panel genes in `X`, per-cell
segmentation metadata in `obs`, and the blank codewords kept apart in `obsm["blank"]`. The
raw counts are copied to a layer, because normalization later overwrites `X`. The table
has neither a transcript count nor a gene count, so both are derived here, over the real
genes only; blank codewords are not counted. `transcript_count` is a cell's total counts
and `gene_count` is how many genes it has at least one count for.

```{python}
adata = ad.read_h5ad(TABLE)

# The sample id comes from inside the object, never from the staged file name.
assert adata.obs["sample"].nunique() == 1, "one table must hold exactly one sample"
SAMPLE = str(adata.obs["sample"].iat[0])

adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()
adata.obs["transcript_count"] = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"].sum(axis=1)).ravel()
adata.obs["gene_count"] = np.asarray((adata.layers["counts"] > 0).sum(axis=1)).ravel()

print(f"{SAMPLE}: {adata.n_obs:,} cells x {adata.n_vars} genes")
```

## B2. Transcripts and genes per cell

How deeply each cell was read. The red line is Phase C's low count cut; it only marks what
that cut would remove. The x-axis runs to each distribution's maximum, so the sparse high
tail is on the plot.

```{python}
transcripts = adata.obs["transcript_count"]
genes = adata.obs["gene_count"]

medians = {"transcripts": np.median(transcripts), "genes": np.median(genes)}
share_below_cut = (transcripts < LOW_COUNT_CUT).mean()

plot_counts_per_cell(transcripts, genes, medians, LOW_COUNT_CUT, share_below_cut)
plt.show()
print(f"maximum: {transcripts.max():.0f} transcripts, {genes.max()} genes")
```

## B3. Cell volume

How large the segmented cells are. A fragment would show as a cluster of very small cells,
and a merge of two cells as a cluster of very large ones. `volume` is in cubic micrometres;
the table's `volume_voxels` is the same measure in voxels, at 0.0175 µm³ per voxel. Nothing
is cut on volume.

```{python}
volume = adata.obs["volume"]

plot_cell_volume(volume, volume.median())
plt.show()
print(f"range: {volume.min():.1f} to {volume.max():.0f} µm³")
```

## B4. Blank codewords against real genes

Blank codewords are probes that should never bind anything, so the counts they collect are
the noise floor. The left panel puts each blank codeword beside each real gene by its total
counts across the section, and shows how far the genes sit above the blanks and whether any
single blank stands out. The right panel shows how many blank counts a single cell
collects, which is how much stray signal one cell carries. Both are looked at, not cut on.

```{python}
blank = adata.obsm["blank"]

gene_totals = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"].sum(axis=0)).ravel()
blank_totals = blank.sum(axis=0).to_numpy()
blank_per_cell = blank.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
cells_per_blank_count = np.bincount(blank_per_cell.astype(int))

plot_blank_codewords(gene_totals, blank_totals, cells_per_blank_count)
plt.show()

blank_share = blank_per_cell.sum() / (blank_per_cell.sum() + adata.obs["transcript_count"].sum())
print(f"blank codewords are {blank_share:.2%} of all counts")
print(
    f"median codeword: {np.median(gene_totals):.0f} counts for real genes, "
    f"{np.median(blank_totals):.0f} for blanks ({np.median(gene_totals) / np.median(blank_totals):.1f}x)"
)
for label, cut in [("median", np.median(blank_totals)), ("95th percentile", np.quantile(blank_totals, 0.95))]:
    print(f"real genes below the blank {label} ({cut:.0f}): {(gene_totals < cut).sum()} of {len(gene_totals)}")
```

## B5. Transcript count on tissue

Where in the section cells were read poorly. Each dot is a cell, coloured by its transcript
count. The curves on the top and right edges are the mean transcripts per cell along x and
along y, in 10 µm bins; they share the map's axes, so a dip sits directly over the part of the
tissue it comes from. The red lines on the curves are where the imaging fields of view's
columns and rows start and end. Where the mean dips on a line, cells along that
field-of-view boundary were read less deeply; a wide, smooth fall towards the border of the
tissue is a different thing, the edge. Nothing is cut on either.

```{python}
xy = np.asarray(adata.obsm["spatial"])
transcripts = adata.obs["transcript_count"].to_numpy()


def mean_by_bin(coord, values, width=10, min_cells=20):
    """Mean of values in bins along one axis; bins with too few cells are left blank."""
    edges = np.arange(coord.min(), coord.max() + width, width)
    idx = np.clip(np.digitize(coord, edges) - 1, 0, len(edges) - 2)
    n = np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(edges) - 1)
    total = np.bincount(idx, weights=values, minlength=len(edges) - 1)
    mean = np.divide(total, n, out=np.full(len(n), np.nan), where=n >= min_cells)
    return edges[:-1] + width / 2, mean


def column_starts(edge, gap=100):
    """Where each column (or row) of fields of view starts: edges within `gap` µm are one."""
    v = np.sort(edge.round(-1).unique())
    return np.array([s for i, s in enumerate(v) if i == 0 or s - v[i - 1] > gap])


fov = pd.read_csv(FOV_EXTENTS, index_col="fov")
fov_size = float(np.median(fov.x_max - fov.x_min))
x_starts, y_starts = column_starts(fov.x_min), column_starts(fov.y_min)
x_bounds = np.sort(np.concatenate([x_starts, x_starts + fov_size]))
y_bounds = np.sort(np.concatenate([y_starts, y_starts + fov_size]))

plot_transcripts_on_tissue(
    xy, transcripts, np.quantile(transcripts, 0.99),
    mean_by_bin(xy[:, 0], transcripts), mean_by_bin(xy[:, 1], transcripts),
    x_bounds, y_bounds,
)
plt.show()
print(f"{len(fov)} fields of view, about {fov_size:.0f} µm square")
```
